rationale: The paper explicitly states that this experiment used a representative US population sample; methods describe recruitment from residential addresses covering US households.
The research-design section identifies three experimental samples: United States (1226), Great Britain (1697), and Germany (1129). At least one experimental sample is explicitly US based.

Study 1 includes an experimental elite sample constructed from mailing lists of Capitol Hill staffers and other professionals. This US legislative recruitment context supports US inference; residence is not stated explicitly, and MTurk or Lucid alone do not establish geography. Classification harmonized to US_inferred for consistency with other institutional-context reviews.

The experiments ask respondents to choose rules for a US town election with Democratic and Republican endorsements. In the surrounding account of American voting attitudes this supports a US participant inference; Verasight alone is not used as geographic evidence. This is an author-linked manuscript of the matching article.
The Samples and Stimuli section expressly describes the experimental SSI sample as representative of the US adult population; analyses cover 1122 partisans.

The Survey Experiment section describes randomized US-city news stories and an outcome about expanding US labor-union influence, within an investigation of Americans' responses to inequality. This supports an inferred US experimental sample; the MTurk platform alone does not establish residence.

The experiment measures respondents' own willingness to pay additional yearly taxes for US government climate preparations and benchmarks the sample's Democratic/Republican identification. This supports an inferred US taxpayer/public sample; respondent residence is not explicitly specified and MTurk is not treated as geographic proof.
